Traditional transparent watercolour painting on rough cold-pressed watercolour paper: a hand-painted background for a 2D narrative adventure game. Technique: loose wet-in-wet washes that bleed softly into one another, then a few transparent glazes laid over the dried washes; the white of the paper shines through every colour and is left completely unpainted for the brightest lights; hard, slightly darker pigment rims where a wash dried (tide lines, small blooms and backruns); visible paper grain and pigment granulation, especially in the blue and violet washes; a few dry-brush strokes on stone and wood. Strong simplification: large simple shapes, few objects, details only suggested with one or two brush marks, soft lost edges in the distance and a few crisp edges in front, no fine lines, no pen or ink outlines, no hatching. Limited palette of transparent pigments: ultramarine blue, indigo, quinacridone rose, burnt sienna, raw sienna and a little sap green; a dusk mood but light, airy values, nothing pitch black, shadows are transparent blue-violet glazes. It must look like a real watercolour painted by hand on paper: not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a digital painting, not oil or gouache, not a postcard, no heavy saturated sunset, no dramatic lighting effects.

Composition for a wide game screen (the picture will be cropped a little at the top and bottom), eye-level side view across the harbour: the horizon lies a little below the middle of the picture. The cottage stands at the left edge, the lighthouse on its low rocky headland at about three quarters of the width, the jetty with the two boats in the middle distance between them, open sea at the right edge. The lighthouse is short and stout and its top stays well below the upper quarter of the picture, with open sky above it; the masts of the boats are short. The iron lantern on its wooden post stands at the back edge of the quay a little right of the middle of the picture. The lower fifth of the picture is a broad, plain, empty strip of quay paving across the full width, seen from slightly above, where characters will walk; the barrels, the crates and the rope stand at the back edge of the quay next to the water, not on this strip. The painting fills the whole sheet to all four edges (no white border, no vignette, no frame).

Location: the small harbour of Lornholm, a fictional island in a northern sea, at dusk. A stone quay with a short wooden jetty runs along the lower third of the picture. Two small wooden fishing boats are moored at the jetty. On a rocky headland on the right stands a white lighthouse with one red band, its lamp lit. On the left a small stone harbour-master's cottage with a lit window and a smoking chimney. On the quay: two barrels, a stack of crates, a coil of rope and an iron lantern on a wooden post. Calm sea, low clouds, a band of orange light at the horizon, the first stars.

Important for the game version: some things move in the game and are added later as separate animated layers, so paint them exactly as described here, even where the description above says otherwise. No smoke at all above the chimney: the chimney top stands clean against the sky. The lighthouse lamp only as a small warm spot of bare paper with a touch of yellow, without any light beam, rays or halo. The lit window and the lantern only as small warm spots, without large glows. The sky a soft wet-in-wet gradient with only a few faint, low cloud streaks near the horizon and no large clouds; the first stars only as a few tiny specks of white paper. The water calm, with only a few soft horizontal strokes and reflections. No birds.

Leave the quay in the foreground free of characters: it is a game background, characters are added later as separate sprites.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.

Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, painted by hand in watercolour. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the painting changes. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image only shows the watercolour technique and the palette of the game: do not copy anything of its content.

No pen or ink outlines, no black contour lines, no hatching, no airbrush gradients, no glossy highlights. The colours of the figures are opaque against the background: the background colour never shows through or tints the figures. Clear, readable colours: cap and vest a clear dark green, the shirt cream, the scarf red, satchel and parcel warm brown, the fur dark grey-brown and creamy white, the broad black-and-white stripes of the face clearly readable, small dark eyes. Soft, even light from the upper left, mid-light values, no backlight, no rim light, no glow around the figure. It must look like a real watercolour painted by hand: not a 3D render, not a digital painting, not a plush toy, not a cartoon with outlines.

Each figure isolated on a fully transparent background, with clear empty space between the figures; no ground, no cast shadow, no frame borders, no paper texture around the figures, nothing cut off at the edge of the sheet.
